current_leader.name: Card authorization integrity-fee prevention engine
current_leader.state_transition: approved card authorization -> no matching clearing/reversal as scheme deadline approaches -> detect fee-triggering stale state -> recommend capture/reverse/leave based on merchant order state -> verify scheme integrity fee avoided
current_leader.why_survived: Visa and Mastercard impose explicit integrity/misuse fees when approved authorizations are not cleared or reversed within defined windows. Payment systems expose authorization/capture/reversal states and webhooks/APIs, creating an independent machine trigger. The narrow wedge can remain read-only by identifying stale authorizations and recommending the exact action before the fee deadline. Current searches found broad payment optimization and fee-audit products, but no dominant exact product focused on cross-PSP pre-deadline authorization-integrity fee prevention.
strongest_evidence: Mastercard introduced/raised time-based and processing-integrity fees in 2026; Moneris documents a 0.0339% fee for cleared approved final transactions submitted 72-168 hours after authorization and fees for unreversed/uncleared preauthorizations.
Visa misuse/integrity fees apply to approved authorizations lacking matching clearing or reversal; merchant guidance requires timely reversals/settlement.
Braintree explicitly warns merchants to void authorized transactions they do not intend to settle to avoid misuse-of-authorization fees.
Adyen and Braintree expose authorization/capture/reversal lifecycle states and APIs; Adyen documents late capture can incur scheme/interchange fees.
current_leader.closest_threat: Broad payment-optimization/orchestration suites, interchange/scheme-fee auditors, and processor-native lifecycle tooling could absorb the feature. Some processors already auto-expire authorizations, but their expiry windows may not align with earlier scheme-fee deadlines; this must be tested per PSP/network/MCC.
current_leader.smallest_intervention: Read PSP authorization/capture/reversal webhooks plus merchant order/fulfillment state. Before each card-network deadline, output one of CAPTURE NOW, REVERSE NOW, or NO ACTION with projected scheme fee avoided. Keep execution merchant-confirmed or optionally invoke the existing PSP reversal/capture endpoint under explicit authorization; never route or custody funds.
current_leader.monetization: Per prevented-fee event, low monthly monitoring fee, or capped percentage of verified scheme integrity fees avoided. Verified savings can be reconciled against processor/network fee reports.
current_leader.biggest_unresolved_risk: Processor-native auto-expiry/reversal behavior may already prevent most fees for common PSPs, and fee rules differ by network, region, MCC and authorization type. Broad enterprise payment-optimization vendors may already cover the same narrow control even if not marketed separately.
current_leader.next_research_test: Switch to ATTACK only if cross-PSP evidence shows material recurring integrity-fee incidence. Quantify fee incidence per 100k authorizations, map exact deadlines by Visa/Mastercard/PSP/MCC, and search enterprise payment-operations products for automatic stale-authorization reversal or pre-deadline fee prevention. Kill if processors already neutralize most exposure or exact incumbent coverage is widespread.

new_search_rules: Prefer fee rules with explicit machine deadlines over annual rightsizing decisions: deadline-driven penalties create higher intervention frequency and cleaner counterfactual attribution.
Processor auto-expiry is not equivalent to fee prevention unless the expiry/reversal occurs before the card-network fee deadline for the applicable authorization type/MCC.
For payment-network fee wedges, a read-only alert plus merchant-confirmed existing PSP action can satisfy non-ownership of the rail; avoid introducing a routing/orchestration proxy.
persistence_scope: Revenue-opportunity research only; unrelated personal/reminder/project tasks are excluded from this opportunity database.
